thread:
devon: FYI hitting a set of decrypt failures on the on-prem cluster after last night's RBAC tighten. traffic to keystore-proxy shows 403s and our audit logs don't have matching identity fetch entries. anyone else seeing this?
anya: which changes went out last night? was it the svcacc role binding we merged?
michael: we merged PR 1692 that scoped the keystore-reader ClusterRole to only the keystore-agent SA and removed the permissive "privileged-keys" binding. intended, but maybe we missed a legacy serviceaccount.
devon: logs from inference-pod-3 show: 
```
[2026-03-22T20:03:11Z] keystore-client WARN call=Decrypt err="remote: HTTP 403 Forbidden" request_id=7c2b
[2026-03-22T20:03:11Z] proxy_resp status=403 body="forbidden: missing key.read permission for svc-account=svc-inference"
```
anya: that error implies the pod's SA isn't in the new binding. devon can you `kubectl get pod -o jsonpath` the pod's serviceAccountName?
devon: svc-inference-sa — but hold on: our audit pipeline is missing the proxy auth entries that normally show who requested the decrypt. checked the proxy logs and they're present, but the central audit index doesn't have them for 20:00-20:30 window.
sara: could be a log-forwarder filter we added to drop low-severity auth logs. I remember a rule to reduce noise that might have been too aggressive. ops-kate, infra-eli any recent logfilter changes?
ops-kate: yeah we pushed a new fluentd config to drop "auth.debug" messages in priv clusters (PR 1720). it was supposed to only affect debug level, but looks like the proxy is emitting auth entries at info and they got grouped. rolling that back now.
sec-bot: alert: multiple 403 decrypts detected across namespace priv-onprem-main (count=43 in 30m). ticket=SEC-2026-322 auto-created. severity=high if >100.
michael: parallel track: we need to identify which SA should have key.read. run: 
```
kubectl get rolebinding -n priv-onprem-main -o wide | grep keystore
kubectl get clusterrolebinding | grep keystore
```
devon: running now, found a legacy rolebinding "keystore-legacy-binding" that binds group:system:authenticated to keystore-reader. looks like PR 1692 removed it but the rolebinding was left behind with a different name.
anya: interesting. maybe some pods still rely on the legacy group. we should: 1) add a temporary emergency binding for svc-inference-sa until we patch image, 2) roll back the fluentd filter so audit logs are retained, 3) enumerate pods using the old SA/group.
infra-eli: i'll push the emergency binding and a targeted configmap to set LOG_FORWARD_AUTH=true for the proxy so entries will be sent even while fluentd fix lands.
sara: also capture the exact missing audit schema fields we need. propose fields: timestamp, pod, namespace, serviceaccount, request_type, key_id, auth_result, callstack(optional).  Add a sample Kibana query: 
```
proxy.logs:auth_result:forbidden AND k8s.namespace:priv-onprem-main | group by serviceaccount | count > 0
```
ops-kate: fluentd rollback PR created -> https://git.company/pr/1755 rolling to 3 nodes. will monitor.
devon: after emergency binding added the decrypts dropped to normal. confirming there are ~0 403s now.
anya: we still need vuln triage: why did image/caller depend on a broader group? could be pre-bootstrapped manifest. open a vuln ticket and label P3 if it's just missing binding, escalate to P2 if automation created the legacy binding.
sec-bot: ticket updated: SEC-2026-322 severity=P2 state=investigating assignees=devon,infra-eli due=2026-03-25.
michael: action items: - emergency binding -> done - revert fluentd filter -> in progress - list pods using legacy SA/group and set migration plan - add audit schema & retention change request - update private-deploy checklist to validate no pods rely on system:authenticated for key access
infra-eli: one more wrinkle: we rotated the keystore-proxy TLS cert yesterday. some older clients still have cached cert pin which may return a handshake error rather than 403. i saw 495/ERR_SSL on a couple of older nodes. i'm adding a short compatibility window to accept both cert v1/v2.
devon: good catch, i did see one pod with TLS handshake failures earlier in the logs. could explain intermittent errors separate from RBAC.
anya: let's keep those separated in the incident writeup. RBAC/rolebinding is the primary mitigation. TLS pinning is secondary and we should announce rotation windows next time.
sara: post-incident: create a runbook entry for rolebinding cleanup and audit verification steps (with commands and sample queries). include a checklist for cert rotation: preflight, compatibility window, monitor queries.
ops-kate: monitoring: adding an alert for (rate(proxy_resp{status="403"}[5m]) > 5) AND cluster=priv-onprem-main. also a monitor for log-forwarder drop-rate > 0.5%
sec-bot: resolution=mitigated_emergency_binding applied; watch_window=72h; links=[SEC-2026-322, https://git.company/pr/1755]
michael: i'll draft the incident summary and include timeline+rootcause+remediation. will ping legal/compliance for any reporting obligations since private-deploy customer clusters were affected.
devon: thanks. closing loop when PRs merged and monitors stable for 72h.
